examples.trans: The white one? Give me the keys.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'grandson' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Hello, Vikulya! And where is our grandson?

meanings.note: By chance or at a station. Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'третить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to meet', paired with 'встречать'.

examples.text: А почему этот серьёзный человек тебя не встретил?
examples.trans: Then why didn't this important man meet you at the station?
I'll meet you at the station.
Yesterday I met an old friend.

meanings.note: In 'до встречи' = until we meet. Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'треча'). Common feminine noun meaning 'meeting' in everyday Russian.
In 'до встречи' = until we meet. Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'треча'). Common feminine noun meaning 'meeting' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Решается ваш вопрос, Клавдия Викторовна! Вы не видите, у меня встреча?
examples.trans: Your question is being sorted out, Klavdia Viktorovna! Can't you see I have a meeting?

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'игрывать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to win'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и выигрывать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to win on time.

meanings.note: Location; for direction use 'куда'. Core Russian adv meaning 'where' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: В гости = for a visit. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guest, visitor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, к вам гости! Па-пам!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, you have visitors! Ta-da!

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.
Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: + instrumental: заняться деньгами = to take care of the money

examples.trans: I will take care of this question tomorrow.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'hotel lobby' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: Comparative of хорошо. Core Russian adv meaning 'better' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I'll be there in ten minutes.

examples.trans: All right, stay there. I'll be there in ten minutes.

meanings.note: + genitive plural: много дел. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Asking permission. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

meanings.note: Agrees with the thing owned. Core Russian det meaning 'my, mine' in everyday speech.

+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Parenthetical adverb. Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'верное').

examples.trans: Well, probably somewhere in the archive.
He has probably already come home.

examples.text: Наверное, что-то серьёзное у вас. Девочка уже две недели лежит в областной клинике!
examples.trans: It must be something serious for you. The girl has been lying in the regional clinic for two weeks already!

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Надо + infinitive. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'сладиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to enjoy, savor'.

examples.text: А можно просто насладиться минутой тишины.
examples.trans: Or one can simply enjoy a minute of silence.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и насладиться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to enjoy on time.

meanings.note: + imperfective infinitive or + accusative

examples.text: Это хорошо, что готово. А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
examples.trans: It's good that it's ready. We were starting to worry.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чинать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to begin, to start', paired with 'начать'.

examples.text: Аркаш, ну что скажешь? Когда начинать?
examples.trans: Arkasha, so what do you say? When do I start?

meanings.note: Used as an exclamation of approval. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'лично'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Отлично, Ваня! Вот это твой образ!
examples.trans: Perfect, Vanya! That right there is your look!

meanings.note: Handing something over. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').

meanings.note: 'это просто' = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

проходить.gloss: to go through; to come in

meanings.note: 'Проходите!' = Come in! (inviting a guest)

Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go through; to come in', paired with 'пройти'.

examples.text: Вика, Паша! Как я рад. Проходите, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Vika, Pasha! I'm so glad. Come in, please.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'порт'). Common masculine noun meaning 'sport, sports' in everyday Russian.

meanings.en: way, method, means of doing something

examples.trans: We found a simple way to solve the problem.
Then listen, there is a clever way.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ыграть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to play'.

examples.trans: The actor played his role wonderfully.

examples.text: Ладно, я попробую сыграть эту роль.
examples.trans: Okay, I will try to play this role.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'низить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to humiliate, belittle'.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'скакать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'galloped off, dashed off'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и ускакать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and galloped off on time.

meanings.note: Играть в шахматы = to play chess. Common plural-only noun meaning 'chess' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: В шахматы умеешь играть? Я научу!
examples.trans: Do you know how to play chess? I'll teach you!
